Please solve this issue: Deleting a book is supposed to leave a permanent record of who had access to
it at that moment: the `Book` model writes one row per person into the
`access_archives` table (`AccessArchive`), so an administrator can later see
who lost what. It has never worked — the archive always comes out empty, no
matter how many people the book was shared with. Deletion itself is fine: the
book and its access grants are removed as expected.

Fix it so that deleting a book through the app writes exactly one archive row
for every person who had access at the moment of deletion, recording the user
and their access level (reader or editor) as it stood. Nothing may be written
before the deletion happens, and someone whose access was revoked earlier must
not appear.

A book nobody had access to gets no rows at all, and that holds however such a
book ends up deleted — even directly from the console. The book and its access
grants still go, exactly as today.

class Book < ApplicationRecord
  include Accessable, Sluggable

  has_many :leaves, dependent: :destroy
  has_one_attached :cover, dependent: :purge_later

  before_destroy :archive_access_list

  scope :ordered, -> { order(:title) }
  scope :published, -> { where(published: true) }

  enum :theme, %w[ black blue green magenta orange violet white ].index_by(&:itself), suffix: true, default: :blue

  def press(leafable, leaf_params)
    leaves.create! leaf_params.merge(leafable: leafable)
  end

  def markable
    leaves.active.positioned.map { it.leafable.markable }.join("\n\n")
  end

  private
    def archive_access_list
      accesses.each do |access|
        AccessArchive.create!(
          book_id: id,
          book_title: title,
          user_id: access.user_id,
          user_name: access.user.name,
          level: access.level
        )
      end
    end
end

class Book < ApplicationRecord
  include Accessable, Sluggable

  has_many :leaves, dependent: :destroy
  has_one_attached :cover, dependent: :purge_later

  # Accessable's `dependent: :destroy` on accesses runs as a before_destroy
  # callback, so the grants must be captured before it removes them.
  before_destroy :capture_access_list, prepend: true
  after_destroy :archive_access_list

  scope :ordered, -> { order(:title) }
  scope :published, -> { where(published: true) }

  enum :theme, %w[ black blue green magenta orange violet white ].index_by(&:itself), suffix: true, default: :blue

  def press(leafable, leaf_params)
    leaves.create! leaf_params.merge(leafable: leafable)
  end

  def markable
    leaves.active.positioned.map { it.leafable.markable }.join("\n\n")
  end

  private
    def capture_access_list
      @access_list = accesses.includes(:user).to_a
    end

    def archive_access_list
      @access_list.each do |access|
        AccessArchive.create!(
          book_id: id,
          book_title: title,
          user_id: access.user_id,
          user_name: access.user.name,
          level: access.level
        )
      end
    end
end

messages.content:
The fix is in place and verified. Deleting a book now writes one archive row per person who had access at that moment, with their name and level.

**Root cause:** `Book` includes `Book::Accessable`, which declares `has_many :accesses, dependent: :destroy`. That option registers a `before_destroy` callback, and it was registered before the model's own `before_destroy :archive_access_list`. So the grants were already deleted when the archive loop ran, and it iterated over nothing.

**The fix** (`app/models/book.rb`):
- `before_destroy :capture_access_list, prepend: true` runs ahead of the grant cleanup and snapshots the current grants, with users loaded.
- `after_destroy :archive_access_list` writes the rows from that snapshot. This happens after the book row is deleted and inside the same transaction as the destroy, so a failed deletion leaves no archive rows.

Revoked grants are already gone from the table, so they never appear. A book with no grants produces an empty snapshot and no rows, with no error. Deletion through the controller, `destroy`, `destroy!`, and `destroy_all` all go through this path.

**Tests:** I added model tests in `test/models/book_test.rb` and a controller test in `test/controllers/books_controller_test.rb`. They cover:
- one row per grant, with the correct name, level and title;
- the book and grants still being removed;
- revoking access writing nothing;
- revoked users not being archived;
